units.guide: Match abortion method to gestational age and setting. Focus for this checkpoint: Abortion methods, Second-trimester abortion. It also includes Second-trimester abortion & Hysterotomy.

Focus for this checkpoint: Medical abortion, Mifepristone mechanism, Misoprostol mechanism, Medical abortion protocol.

questions.q: Which first-trimester medical-abortion combination is listed?
questions.exp: First-trimester medical abortion uses mifepristone plus misoprostol. (Book p428)

questions.q: What setting is stated for first-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: First-trimester medical abortion is managed on an OPD basis. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which surgical method is listed for first-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Suction evacuation is a listed first-trimester method. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which method is especially listed for rural areas in the first trimester?
questions.exp: MVA is listed for rural areas. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which first-trimester method is described as outdated?
questions.exp: Menstrual regulation is marked outdated. (Book p428)

questions.q: What setting is stated for second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: Second-trimester medical abortion is an inpatient procedure. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which prostaglandin is listed as an option for second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: Misoprostol is listed among second-trimester prostaglandin options. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which non-prostaglandin medication is listed for second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: Oxytocin is a listed second-trimester medical-abortion option. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which instillation method is listed for second-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Extra-amniotic ethacridine instillation is listed. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which intra-amniotic procedure is listed for second-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Intra-amniotic saline is listed as a second-trimester option. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which surgical methods are listed for second-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Suction evacuation and D&E are listed surgical options in the second trimester. (Book p428)

questions.q: What is a hysterotomy in the context of MTP?
opts: Opening the uterus to remove products of conception
Closing the cervix with a cerclage
questions.exp: Hysterotomy means opening the uterus to take out products of conception. (Book p428)

questions.q: Up to what gestation is first-trimester medical abortion stated to be used?
questions.exp: First-trimester medical abortion is used up to 9 weeks or 63 days. (Book p428)

questions.q: What route is used for mifepristone in the source protocol?
questions.exp: Mifepristone is administered orally. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which routes are listed for misoprostol?
questions.exp: Misoprostol may be oral, sublingual, per-vaginal, or per-rectal. (Book p428)

questions.q: What is the mechanism of mifepristone (RU-486) in medical abortion?
opts: Progesterone antagonism causing detachment of implanted embryo
Oxytocin agonism causing uterine contractions only
questions.exp: Mifepristone is a progesterone antagonist that detaches the implanted embryo. (Book p428)

questions.q: What is the mechanism of misoprostol in medical abortion?
opts: It promotes uterine contraction and cervical ripening/softening to expel the detached embryo
questions.exp: Misoprostol causes uterine contractions and cervical ripening to expel the detached embryo. (Book p428)

questions.q: After which drug does bleeding occur in the first-trimester medical-abortion protocol?
questions.exp: Bleeding occurs after misoprostol. (Book p428)

questions.q: What is the day-1 drug and dose in the source medical-abortion protocol?
opts: Mifepristone 200 mg as one oral tablet
questions.exp: Day 1 is a single 200-mg oral mifepristone tablet. (Book p428)

questions.q: What is the day-3 drug and dose in the source protocol?
questions.exp: Day 3 is misoprostol 800 micrograms. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which route order is preferred for 800-microgram misoprostol in the source protocol?
questions.exp: The source gives vaginal > sublingual > oral; oral has more side effects. (Book p428)

questions.q: When does bleeding usually occur after the day-3 misoprostol dose?
questions.exp: Bleeding generally occurs 4–6 hours after misoprostol. (Book p428)

questions.q: When is follow-up scheduled to ensure complete abortion in the source protocol?
questions.exp: Follow-up is on day 15 to ensure complete abortion. (Book p428)

questions.q: Is ultrasound routinely required in MTP?
questions.exp: USG is not routinely required in MTP. (Book p428)

questions.q: When is ultrasound indicated before/around medical abortion?
opts: Uncertain LMP or uterine size not matching period of gestation
Every patient with a known LMP and matching size
questions.exp: USG is indicated if LMP is uncertain or uterine size does not match gestational age. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which symptom is an ultrasound indication in medical abortion?
questions.exp: Abdominal pain is an indication for USG. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which day-15 finding is an ultrasound indication in medical abortion?
opts: No symptoms with a closed internal os
Continuous P/V spotting with an open internal os
questions.exp: Continuous spotting P/V with an open os on day 15 prompts USG. (Book p428)

questions.q: Which hemoglobin level is a contraindication to medical abortion in the notes?
questions.exp: Hb below 8 g/dL is listed as a contraindication. (Book p429)

questions.q: Why is inability to comply with follow-up a contraindication to medical abortion?
opts: The regimen requires assessment of completion and timely management of failure
questions.exp: Patients must be able to comply with follow-up for medical abortion. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which blood-pressure state is a listed contraindication to medical abortion?
opts: Uncontrolled hypertension at or above 160/100 mmHg
questions.exp: Uncontrolled HTN ≥160/100 mmHg is listed as a contraindication. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which neurological condition is a listed contraindication to medical abortion?
questions.exp: Uncontrolled seizures are a listed contraindication. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which endocrine/metabolic disorder is a listed contraindication to medical abortion?
questions.exp: Chronic adrenal failure is listed as a contraindication. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which two conditions are listed as contraindications to medical abortion?
opts: Rh negativity and hypertension controlled on medication
questions.exp: Porphyria and glaucoma are listed contraindications. (Book p429)

questions.q: What complication may require surgical MTP after medical abortion?
opts: A normal expected brief bleed only
questions.exp: Excessive bleeding and incomplete abortion can require surgical MTP. (Book p429)

questions.q: If no bleeding occurs within 24 hours after misoprostol, what is the next assessment?
questions.exp: No bleeding after 24 hours prompts USG to assess cardiac activity. (Book p429)

questions.q: If cardiac activity is present after a nonbleeding medical-abortion course, what is the management?
questions.exp: If cardiac activity is present, it is a live pregnancy and S&E is performed. (Book p429)

questions.q: If cardiac activity is absent after a nonbleeding medical-abortion course, what is the next step?
opts: Repeat 400–800 micrograms misoprostol and follow up after 7 days
questions.exp: Absent cardiac activity leads to repeat 400–800 micrograms misoprostol and review after 7 days. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which pre-assessment test is included before medical abortion?
questions.exp: Pre-assessment includes hemoglobin, urine routine/microscopy, ABO/Rh group, and pregnancy test if not already done. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which blood test/grouping is included in pre-assessment for medical abortion?
questions.exp: ABO/Rh grouping is part of the pre-assessment. (Book p429)

questions.q: What is the best method of MTP between 9 and 12 weeks according to the notes?
questions.exp: Suction evacuation is described as the best MTP method at 9–12 weeks. (Book p429)

questions.q: Up to what gestation can suction evacuation be performed according to the notes?
questions.exp: Suction evacuation can be done up to 16 weeks. (Book p429)

questions.q: What instrument is used to dilate the internal os before suction evacuation?
questions.exp: Hegar's dilators are used to dilate the internal os. (Book p429)

questions.q: What instrument evacuates products of conception during suction evacuation?
opts: MVA syringe alone in all settings
Karman's cannula attached to a suction machine
questions.exp: Karman's cannula is attached to the suction machine to evacuate products of conception. (Book p429)

questions.q: What is the first procedural step in suction evacuation?
questions.exp: The first procedural step is to empty the bladder. (Book p429)

questions.q: Why is P/V examination performed in lithotomy before suction evacuation?
opts: To confirm uterine size and position, anteverted or retroverted
questions.exp: P/V examination confirms uterine size and position. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which instrument retracts the posterior vaginal wall during suction evacuation?
questions.exp: Sim's speculum retracts the posterior vaginal wall. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which instrument retracts the anterior vaginal wall during suction evacuation?
questions.exp: An anterior vaginal-wall retractor is used for the anterior wall. (Book p429)

questions.q: Which instrument can be used to hold the cervix during suction evacuation?
questions.exp: The cervix is held with a vulsellum or sponge-holding forceps. (Book p430)

questions.q: What anesthesia is used for suction evacuation in the notes?
questions.exp: Suction evacuation uses a paracervical block. (Book p430)

questions.q: What are the functions of a uterine sound before suction evacuation?
opts: Measure uterocervical length, confirm uterine position, and act as first dilator
questions.exp: The uterine sound measures uterocervical length, confirms position, and acts as first dilator. (Book p430)

questions.q: When should the suction machine be switched off during use of Karman's cannula?
opts: It should never be switched off
During insertion and removal of the cannula
questions.exp: The suction machine is switched off during Karman cannula insertion and removal. (Book p430)

questions.q: What physical feature characterizes a Karman cannula?
opts: Plastic cannula with two triangular openings
Metal cannula with one circular opening
questions.exp: Karman cannula is plastic and has two triangular openings. (Book p430)

questions.q: What does the number of a Karman cannula indicate?
questions.exp: Cannula number equals its diameter in millimeters. (Book p430)

questions.q: How is Karman cannula size selected from gestational age?
opts: Cannula size equals gestation in weeks or one less
questions.exp: Cannula size is gestational weeks or one less. (Book p430)

questions.q: Which are listed uses of Karman cannula besides S&E?
opts: Incomplete/missed abortion and endometrial biopsy in India
questions.exp: Karman cannula can also treat incomplete/missed abortion and be used for endometrial biopsy in India. (Book p430)

questions.q: What is the maximum Karman cannula number used for suction evacuation?
questions.exp: The maximum KC number used for S&E is 16. (Book p430)

questions.q: What local anesthetic concentration is stated for paracervical block in S&E?
questions.exp: The paracervical block uses 1% lignocaine. (Book p430)

questions.q: At what clock position is anesthetic given for tenaculum placement/holding the cervix?
questions.exp: The 12 o’clock position is the site to hold the cervix. (Book p430)

questions.q: At which clock positions is paracervical anesthetic injected in addition to 12 o’clock?
questions.exp: Injection sites are 2, 4, 8, and 10 o’clock in addition to 12. (Book p430)

questions.q: Why are 3 and 9 o’clock avoided for paracervical block?
opts: They lie on the descending cervical-artery side
questions.exp: The descending cervical artery lies at 3 and 9 o’clock, so those sites are avoided. (Book p430)

questions.q: What suction pressure is generated during S&E according to the notes?
questions.exp: S&E generates a pressure of at least 600 mmHg. (Book p430)

questions.q: Which is an endpoint suggesting completion of suction evacuation?
opts: Decreased blood loss with air bubbles entering the Karman cannula
questions.exp: Endpoints include reduced blood loss and air bubbles in the Karman cannula. (Book p430)

questions.q: What tactile uterine/cannula findings suggest completion of suction evacuation?
opts: Grating over uterus and a closing internal os causing grip on the cannula
Loss of all resistance and deep cannula entry
An open os with POC coming out
questions.exp: Completion brings grating sensation and closing internal os with grip on KC. (Book p430)

questions.q: What is the immediate action if perforation occurs while using a dilator in S&E?
questions.exp: With dilator perforation, stop the procedure and observe. (Book p431)

questions.q: How can perforation with a dilator be prevented?
opts: Hold the dilator in a pen-holding manner
questions.exp: Holding the dilator in a pen-holding manner prevents perforation. (Book p431)

questions.q: Which finding suggests uterine perforation by Karman cannula?
opts: Sudden loss of resistance and the cannula going deep into the uterus
questions.exp: Loss of resistance and deep KC entry identify possible perforation. (Book p431)

questions.q: Which clinical deterioration suggests Karman-cannula perforation?
opts: Raised pulse with falling BP/shock and severe abdominal pain
questions.exp: Perforation can cause shock (raised pulse/falling BP) and severe abdominal pain. (Book p431)

questions.q: What should be done immediately when Karman-cannula perforation is suspected?
opts: Stop procedure, do not remove the cannula, inform senior consultant, and check vitals
questions.exp: Stop, leave KC in place, call senior help, and assess vitals. (Book p431)

questions.q: What diagnostic approach follows suspected Karman-cannula perforation in a stable patient?
questions.exp: A stable patient proceeds to diagnostic laparoscopy. (Book p431)

questions.q: What diagnostic approach follows suspected Karman-cannula perforation in an unstable patient?
questions.exp: An unstable patient receives resuscitative measures plus diagnostic laparotomy. (Book p431)

questions.q: What is the role of manual vacuum aspiration in the notes?
opts: Alternative to S&E in rural areas
A method of fetal anemia testing
questions.exp: MVA is an alternative to S&E in rural areas. (Book p431)

questions.q: What equipment is required for MVA?
opts: MVA syringe and Karman cannula; electricity is not required
Suction machine and general anesthesia only
questions.exp: MVA needs an MVA syringe and KC; electricity is not required. (Book p431)

questions.q: How many pinch valves does the MVA syringe have in the source comparison?
questions.exp: The MVA syringe has two pinch valves. (Book p431)

questions.q: What is the status of menstrual regulation in the source comparison?
questions.exp: Menstrual regulation is marked outdated. (Book p431)

questions.q: How many pinch valves does the menstrual-regulation syringe have?
questions.exp: The MR syringe has a single pinch valve. (Book p431)

questions.q: Which broad options exist for second-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Second-trimester abortion can be medical or surgical. (Book p432)

questions.q: Until what gestation is suction evacuation listed as a surgical option in second-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Suction evacuation is listed up to 16 weeks. (Book p432)

questions.q: What class of drug is best for second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: Prostaglandins are the best drugs for second-trimester medical abortion. (Book p432)

questions.q: Which prostaglandin is described as best for second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: Misoprostol, a PGE1 analogue, is listed as best. (Book p432)

questions.q: What second-trimester misoprostol regimen is given?
questions.exp: The regimen is misoprostol 400 micrograms every 3 hours, maximum five doses. (Book p432)

questions.q: What setting is required for second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: The patient should be admitted for second-trimester medical abortion. (Book p432)

questions.q: How are products of conception expelled in second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: The patient experiences mini labor and expels the products. (Book p432)

questions.q: Which drug is noted as not used in second-trimester medical abortion?
questions.exp: The source notes mifepristone is not used in the second trimester. (Book p432)

questions.q: What is the most common surgical method of second-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: D&E is the most common surgical method. (Book p432)

questions.q: Which instruments are used for dilatation and evacuation?
questions.exp: D&E uses ovum forceps or sponge-holding forceps. (Book p432)

questions.q: What is done after the D&E procedure in the notes?
questions.exp: Blunt curettage is done after D&E. (Book p432)

questions.q: Which forceps have no ratchet lock?
questions.exp: Ovum forceps have no ratchet lock; sponge-holding forceps have ratchet locks. (Book p432)

questions.q: What curettage rule is stated for a pregnant uterus?
opts: Only do curettage in the first trimester
questions.exp: In a pregnant uterus, blunt curettage is always done. (Book p432)

questions.q: What is the exception to the blunt-curettage rule in a pregnant uterus?
opts: After suction evacuation of molar pregnancy
questions.exp: The exception is after S&E of molar pregnancy. (Book p432)

questions.q: Why should pregnancy not be continued after failed second-trimester medical abortion with misoprostol?
opts: Misoprostol is teratogenic and can cause Möbius syndrome
questions.exp: Misoprostol is teratogenic and is linked to Möbius syndrome, so pregnancy should not continue. (Book p432)

questions.q: In ectopic pregnancy, what structure secretes progesterone?
questions.exp: In ectopic pregnancy, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone while placenta is absent. (Book p433)

questions.q: How do progesterone levels in ectopic pregnancy compare with nonpregnant and intrauterine states?
opts: Lower than nonpregnant and higher than intrauterine pregnancy
Higher than nonpregnant but lower than intrauterine pregnancy
questions.exp: Ectopic progesterone is above nonpregnant level but below intrauterine-pregnancy level. (Book p433)

questions.q: What endometrial ultrasound appearance may result from decidualization in ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Decidualization can create a pseudogestational sac on USG. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is abnormal about decidua vera in ectopic pregnancy?
opts: It differentiates normally into all three layers
It is not differentiated into basalis, capsularis, and parietalis
questions.exp: Decidua vera is present but not differentiated into the normal basalis/capsularis/parietalis layers. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is a decidual cast in ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Decidual cast is shedding of the decidua. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the correct medial-to-lateral order of fallopian-tube parts?
questions.exp: The order from medial to lateral is interstitium (intramural), isthmus, ampulla, then infundibulum. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the narrowest part of the fallopian tube according to the notes?
questions.exp: The narrowest site is interstitium, followed by isthmus. (Book p433)

questions.q: Which fallopian-tube region is the anatomic sphincter?
questions.exp: The anatomic sphincter is the interstitium. (Book p433)

questions.q: Which fallopian-tube region is the physiologic sphincter?
questions.exp: The physiologic sphincter is the isthmus. (Book p433)

questions.q: Which tubal ectopic site lasts longest and why?
opts: Ampulla because it has no plicae
Infundibulum because it has no blood supply
questions.exp: Interstitial ectopic lasts longest due to myometrial support and is most dangerous because of bleeding. (Book p433)

questions.q: Which tubal ectopic site ends earliest?
questions.exp: An isthmic ectopic ends earliest. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the most common site of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: The fallopian tube is the most common site of ectopic pregnancy. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the most common tubal site of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Ampulla is the most common tubal site. (Book p433)

questions.q: Why is ampulla the most common tubal ectopic site according to the notes?
opts: It is the site of fertilization and has the maximum mucosal plicae
questions.exp: Ampulla is the fertilization site and has the most plicae, making it the most common site. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the least common part of the tube for ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Interstitium is the least common tubal ectopic site. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the most common non-tubal site of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Ovary is the most common non-tubal ectopic site. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is the least common ectopic-site order in the source?
opts: Cesarean-scar ectopic, then cervical ectopic, then abdominal ectopic
questions.exp: The source ranks cesarean-scar ectopic > cervical ectopic > abdominal ectopic as least common sites. (Book p433)

questions.q: Why can an abdominal ectopic pregnancy last longest overall?
opts: It derives blood supply from adjacent organs
questions.exp: Abdominal ectopic lasts longest because it derives blood supply from adjacent organs. (Book p433)

questions.q: What is tubal abortion?
opts: Rupture through the uterine cornu only
Expulsion occurring through the fimbrial end of the tube
questions.exp: Tubal abortion occurs in the fimbrial end of the tube. (Book p434)

questions.q: What is the most common site of tubal abortion?
questions.exp: Ampulla is the most common site of tubal abortion. (Book p434)

questions.q: What is tubal rupture due to in ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Continuous growth of the ectopic gestation
Immediate loss of the corpus luteum
questions.exp: Tubal rupture results from continuing ectopic growth. (Book p434)

questions.q: What is the most common site of tubal rupture?
questions.exp: Isthmus is the most common site of tubal rupture. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which criteria are used for cervical ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Paalman criteria; Rubin criteria are obsolete
questions.exp: Paalman is the newer cervical-ectopic criteria; Rubin is obsolete. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which criteria are used for primary abdominal ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Primary abdominal ectopic pregnancy uses Studdiford criteria. (Book p434)

questions.q: What does secondary abdominal ectopic pregnancy arise from according to the notes?
questions.exp: Secondary abdominal ectopic arises from the fimbrial end. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which criteria are used for ovarian ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Ovarian ectopic pregnancy uses Spiegelberg criteria. (Book p434)

questions.q: What is the most common risk factor for ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: PID/salpingitis is the most common ectopic risk factor. (Book p434)

questions.q: What risk history carries the highest risk for ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Previous ectopic pregnancy or tubal surgery
questions.exp: Previous ectopic pregnancy or tubal surgery has the highest listed risk. (Book p434)

questions.q: How do PID-related risk factors promote ectopic pregnancy?
opts: They cause adhesions that prevent implantation in the uterus
questions.exp: PID/tubal surgery causes adhesions that prevent normal uterine implantation. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which sexual/infective histories are listed as ectopic risk factors?
questions.exp: Cervicitis and multiple partners are risk factors for PID and ectopic pregnancy. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which lifestyle/obstetric histories are listed ectopic risk factors?
opts: Folic acid use and normal BP
questions.exp: Smoking and prior cesarean section are listed risk factors. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which fertility-related factor increases ectopic pregnancy risk?
questions.exp: Infertility and ART are listed risk factors. (Book p434)

questions.q: What happens to the absolute risk of ectopic pregnancy with contraception overall?
opts: It decreases because the chance of pregnancy decreases
questions.exp: Contraception lowers absolute ectopic risk by lowering overall chance of pregnancy. (Book p434)

questions.q: What happens to relative ectopic risk if a contraceptive method fails?
questions.exp: A contraceptive failure has higher relative likelihood of ectopic pregnancy. (Book p434)

questions.q: Which failed contraceptive method has the highest relative ectopic risk in the source ranking?
questions.exp: Among failed methods, tubal ligation has highest relative ectopic risk. (Book p434)

questions.q: What is the correct relative ectopic-risk order among failed methods in the notes?
opts: Tubal ligation > progesterone IUD > copper IUD
Copper IUD > progesterone IUD > tubal ligation
questions.exp: The source ranks tubal ligation above progesterone IUD (Mirena/Progestasert), above copper IUD. (Book p434)

questions.q: Why do progesterone-only pills carry higher relative ectopic risk than combined OCPs if they fail?
opts: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle and reduces tubal peristalsis
questions.exp: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle and reduces peristalsis, giving POP > OCP relative ectopic risk. (Book p434)

questions.q: What is the classic clinical triad of ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Amenorrhea, abdominal pain, and bleeding per vaginum
questions.exp: The classic ectopic triad is amenorrhea, abdominal pain, and P/V bleeding. (Book p435)

questions.q: What is the most specific and consistent symptom of ectopic pregnancy according to the notes?
questions.exp: Pain is the most specific and consistent ectopic symptom. (Book p435)

questions.q: How is ectopic abdominal pain typically described?
opts: Localized lower abdominal, sharp or dull, and unilateral
questions.exp: Ectopic pain is localized lower abdominal pain that may be sharp/dull and unilateral. (Book p435)

questions.q: At what gestation does an isthmic ectopic commonly terminate?
questions.exp: The timing table lists 6–8 weeks for isthmic ectopic. (Book p435)

questions.q: At what gestation does an ampullary ectopic commonly terminate?
questions.exp: Ampullary ectopic commonly terminates at 8–10 weeks. (Book p435)

questions.q: At what gestation does an interstitial ectopic commonly terminate?
questions.exp: Interstitial ectopic commonly terminates around 12 weeks. (Book p435)

questions.q: What causes mid/upper abdominal pain in a ruptured ectopic?
questions.exp: Hemoperitoneum causes mid/upper abdominal pain in a ruptured ectopic. (Book p435)

questions.q: What is Danforth sign?
opts: Shoulder-tip pain from diaphragmatic irritation by blood
questions.exp: Danforth sign is shoulder-tip pain due to diaphragmatic irritation. (Book p435)

questions.q: Why may a ruptured ectopic cause urge to defecate?
opts: Blood in the cul-de-sac presses on the rectum
questions.exp: Blood in the pouch of Douglas exerts pressure on the rectum, causing urge to defecate. (Book p435)

questions.q: What test result supports the diagnosis of ruptured ectopic pregnancy in the notes?
questions.exp: Ruptured ectopic has a positive UPT. (Book p435)

questions.q: Which finding added to the ectopic triad is suggestive of ruptured ectopic?
questions.exp: Triad plus shoulder-tip pain, urge to defecate, or orthostatic hypotension suggests rupture. (Book p435)

questions.q: What systemic examination finding may be present in ruptured ectopic?
questions.exp: Shock may be present in ruptured ectopic. (Book p435)

questions.q: Which abdominal localizing signs may occur in ruptured ectopic?
opts: Distension, rigidity, guarding, and rebound tenderness
questions.exp: Distension, rigidity, guarding, and rebound tenderness are listed localizing signs. (Book p435)

questions.q: How does uterine size relate to period of gestation in ruptured ectopic?
opts: Exactly equals POG in every case
Enlarged but smaller than period of gestation
Always larger than period of gestation
questions.exp: The uterus is enlarged but smaller than expected for POG. (Book p435)

questions.q: What is the most significant P/V finding in ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Cervical motion tenderness due to peritonitis
questions.exp: Cervical motion tenderness due to peritonitis is the most significant P/V finding. (Book p436)

questions.q: How does UPT help distinguish PID from ectopic pregnancy in a patient with cervical motion tenderness?
opts: PID is always UPT positive and ectopic negative
PID is UPT negative; ectopic is UPT positive with raised beta-hCG
questions.exp: PID is UPT negative, while ectopic is UPT positive/has raised beta-hCG. (Book p436)

questions.q: What initial combination points directly to surgical management of ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Triad plus positive UPT plus localizing signs
questions.exp: The triad with positive UPT and localizing signs proceeds to surgical management. (Book p436)

questions.q: What operative route is preferred for a ruptured ectopic with stable vitals?
questions.exp: Stable vitals permit laparoscopy. (Book p436)

questions.q: What operative route is preferred for a ruptured ectopic with unstable vitals?
questions.exp: Unstable vitals require laparotomy. (Book p436)

questions.q: What is the procedure of choice in ruptured ectopic regardless of family completion?
questions.exp: Salpingectomy is the procedure of choice in ruptured ectopic irrespective of family completion. (Book p436)

questions.q: In which ectopic location is oophorectomy used according to the notes?
questions.exp: Oophorectomy is used only for ovarian ectopic. (Book p436)

questions.q: Which options are contraindicated in ruptured ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Expectant and medical management, and surgery other than salpingectomy
questions.exp: Ruptured ectopic contraindicates expectant/medical care and surgery other than salpingectomy. (Book p436)

questions.q: What is the indication for culdocentesis in the source notes?
questions.exp: Culdocentesis is indicated in ruptured ectopic pregnancy. (Book p436)

questions.q: How is culdocentesis performed?
opts: A needle enters the uterine fundus through abdomen
A cannula enters the cervix only
An arterial line enters the radial artery
A syringe enters the pouch of Douglas through the posterior fornix
questions.exp: A syringe is introduced into the cul-de-sac/pouch of Douglas through the posterior fornix. (Book p436)

questions.q: How does blood aspirated from a blood vessel differ from hemoperitoneum on culdocentesis?
opts: Blood-vessel sample clots, whereas pouch-of-Douglas blood does not clot
questions.exp: Blood in a vessel clots; hemoperitoneum blood in pouch of Douglas lacks clotting factors and does not clot. (Book p436)

questions.q: In amenorrhea with P/V bleeding and abdominal pain, what is the first investigation for ectopic pregnancy?
opts: UPT, positive in about 99% because of beta-hCG
questions.exp: The first step is UPT, positive in about 99% due to beta-hCG. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the investigation of choice after a positive UPT in suspected unruptured ectopic?
questions.exp: TVS is the investigation of choice after positive UPT. (Book p437)

questions.q: What TVS finding is diagnostic of tubal ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Gestational sac with yolk sac in the fallopian tube
questions.exp: A gestational sac plus yolk sac in the tube is diagnostic. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the tubal/bagel sign?
opts: A yolk sac in the uterine cavity
A fallopian-tube gestational sac without a yolk sac
questions.exp: Tubal/bagel sign is a gestational sac in the fallopian tube with no yolk sac. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the ring-of-fire sign in ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Absent all vascularity around the ectopic
questions.exp: Ring of fire is increased vascularity around an ectopic. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the most common inconclusive TVS finding of ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Complex adnexal mass due to areas of hemorrhage
questions.exp: Complex adnexal mass from hemorrhage is the most common inconclusive finding. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the next step after inconclusive ectopic findings on TVS?
questions.exp: Inconclusive TVS leads to beta-hCG measurement. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the critical beta-hCG titre in suspected ectopic pregnancy?
opts: The value at which fetal anemia is detected
The value at which an intrauterine gestational sac should be visible
questions.exp: Critical beta-hCG titre is the level at which an intrauterine sac is visible. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the source-algorithm interpretation of beta-hCG at least 2,000 IU with no intrauterine gestational sac?
opts: Unruptured ectopic pregnancy; use medical management if eligible
questions.exp: Beta-hCG ≥2,000 IU with no sac indicates unruptured ectopic in the algorithm. (Book p437)

questions.q: With beta-hCG below 2,000 IU and an empty uterus, what is the appropriate next step?
opts: Immediately diagnose ectopic in every case
questions.exp: Below the discriminatory level with an empty uterus, repeat beta-hCG after 48 hours. (Book p437)

questions.q: What beta-hCG change after 48 hours is consistent with a live intrauterine pregnancy in the source flowchart?
questions.exp: A near doubling, shown as a 33–60% rise in the source flowchart, supports live IUP. (Book p437)

questions.q: What beta-hCG pattern after 48 hours supports ectopic pregnancy in the source flowchart?
questions.exp: A slow rise below 33% supports ectopic pregnancy. (Book p437)

questions.q: What beta-hCG pattern after 48 hours supports abortion/nonviable intrauterine pregnancy?
questions.exp: Falling beta-hCG supports abortion/nonviable IUP. (Book p437)

questions.q: What is the gold-standard investigation for ectopic pregnancy in the notes?
questions.exp: Laparoscopy is listed as the gold standard. (Book p438)

questions.q: What serum progesterone level supports live intrauterine pregnancy in the source notes?
questions.exp: Serum progesterone ≥25 ng/mL suggests live intrauterine pregnancy. (Book p438)

questions.q: What serum progesterone level supports ectopic pregnancy in the source notes?
questions.exp: Serum progesterone ≤5 ng/mL supports ectopic pregnancy. (Book p438)

questions.q: Which procedure is contraindicated in ectopic pregnancy because it can disrupt the tube?
questions.exp: HSG is listed as contraindicated in ectopic pregnancy. (Book p438)

questions.q: Which other gynecologic procedures are contraindicated in ectopic pregnancy according to the notes?
questions.exp: Hysteroscopy and colpotomy are contraindicated; colpotomy is for pelvic-abscess drainage. (Book p438)

questions.q: What is the preferred/best management branch for an eligible unruptured ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: The management diagram marks medical management as best when eligible. (Book p438)

questions.q: What are indications for surgical management of ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Ruptured ectopic or unruptured ectopic that does not meet medical-management prerequisites
questions.exp: Surgery is indicated for rupture or if an unruptured ectopic fails medical-treatment prerequisites. (Book p438)

questions.q: Which clinical state is required for medical management of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Medical management requires an unruptured ectopic and stable vitals. (Book p438)

questions.q: What beta-hCG level is a prerequisite for medical management of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Medical therapy prerequisite includes beta-hCG below 5,000 IU. (Book p438)

questions.q: What ectopic size is a prerequisite for medical management?
questions.exp: The ectopic site/size must be less than 4 cm. (Book p438)

questions.q: What cardiac-activity finding is a standard prerequisite for medical management?
opts: It has no impact on failure risk
questions.exp: Absence of cardiac activity is a prerequisite. (Book p438)

questions.q: What reproductive preference is included among medical-management prerequisites?
questions.exp: The notes include family not completed among prerequisites. (Book p438)

questions.q: How does fetal cardiac activity affect medical ectopic treatment if ectopic size is below 3.5 cm?
opts: It is not an absolute contraindication, but failure risk is higher
questions.exp: Cardiac activity is not an absolute contraindication if size <3.5 cm, but it raises failure rate. (Book p438)

questions.q: What is the drug of choice for medical management of ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Methotrexate is the drug of choice. (Book p438)

questions.q: What route is used for methotrexate in ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: Methotrexate is administered intramuscularly. (Book p438)

questions.q: What methotrexate dose is listed for ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: The stated dose is 50 mg/m² or 1 mg/kg. (Book p438)

questions.q: How does ectopic-pregnancy methotrexate differ from GTN methotrexate therapy in the source note?
opts: Ectopic uses a full single dose in one day; GTN uses multidose therapy alternating with folinic acid
Both always use the same regimen
questions.exp: Ectopic therapy is single dose; GTN multidose therapy alternates doses on D1/D3/D5/D7 with folinic acid. (Book p438)

questions.q: What is done on day 1 of single-dose methotrexate therapy for ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Measure beta-hCG and administer the entire methotrexate dose
Measure only beta-hCG with no drug
questions.exp: Day 1 includes beta-hCG measurement and the full methotrexate injection. (Book p438)

questions.q: On which days is beta-hCG measured after single-dose methotrexate to estimate response?
questions.exp: Beta-hCG is measured on days 4 and 7. (Book p438)

questions.q: What fall in beta-hCG between day 4 and day 7 indicates successful medical treatment?
questions.exp: A decline of at least 15% from D4 to D7 indicates successful medical therapy. (Book p439)

questions.q: What is done if beta-hCG falls by less than 15% between day 4 and 7 after methotrexate?
opts: Repeat the entire methotrexate dose as a new day 1, up to 3 doses
questions.exp: A <15% fall is inadequate; repeat full MTX as new D1, maximum three doses. (Book p439)

questions.q: What defines failed medical therapy after up to three methotrexate injections?
opts: Day-7 fall less than 15% after three injections or rising hCG from D4 to D7
A 15% fall from D4 to D7
questions.exp: Failure is <15% D7 fall after three injections or rising D4–D7 hCG, requiring surgery. (Book p439)

questions.q: What does a rise in beta-hCG between day 1 and day 3 after methotrexate usually represent?
opts: A normal release from the dying ectopic sac
questions.exp: A D1–D3 hCG rise can be normal due to release from the dying ectopic sac. (Book p439)

questions.q: What is the preferred operative route for surgical management of unruptured ectopic pregnancy?
questions.exp: The surgical-management route listed is laparoscopy. (Book p439)

questions.q: When is linear salpingostomy the surgery of choice for unruptured ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Family complete and ectopic size at least 5 cm
Family not complete and ectopic size under 4 cm
questions.exp: Linear salpingostomy is chosen if family is incomplete and ectopic is <4 cm. (Book p439)

questions.q: What is done in linear salpingostomy?
opts: Incision with hydrodissection; tube left intact and incision left open
questions.exp: Linear salpingostomy uses incision/hydrodissection, preserves tube, and leaves incision open. (Book p439)

questions.q: When is unilateral salpingectomy the surgery of choice for unruptured ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Family complete or ectopic size at least 5 cm
Family incomplete and ectopic below 4 cm
questions.exp: Unilateral salpingectomy is selected if family is complete or ectopic is ≥5 cm. (Book p439)

questions.q: Which tubal procedures are labeled obsolete in the ectopic-surgery notes?
opts: Milking of tubes and salpingotomy with closed incision
questions.exp: Milking tubes and salpingotomy with closed incision are obsolete. (Book p439)

questions.q: What is the indication for expectant management of ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Heterotopic pregnancy with a live IUP
questions.exp: Expectant management is wait and watch for spontaneously resolving ectopic pregnancy. (Book p439)

questions.q: What beta-hCG value is a prerequisite for expectant ectopic management?
questions.exp: Expectant management requires beta-hCG <200 IU. (Book p439)

questions.q: What beta-hCG trend is required for expectant ectopic management?
questions.exp: A spontaneous fall in beta-hCG is required. (Book p439)

questions.q: What ultrasound prerequisite is listed for expectant ectopic management?
opts: No gestational sac in the fallopian tube
Definite yolk sac in the tube
questions.exp: Expectant management requires no gestational sac in the tube. (Book p439)

questions.q: What is heterotopic pregnancy?
opts: A molar pregnancy with a fetus
Twin pregnancy with one intrauterine and one ectopic pregnancy
questions.exp: Heterotopic pregnancy has one IUP and one ectopic pregnancy. (Book p439)

questions.q: Why is methotrexate contraindicated in heterotopic pregnancy?
opts: It would harm the coexisting intrauterine pregnancy
questions.exp: Methotrexate is contraindicated because a desired intrauterine pregnancy coexists. (Book p439)

questions.q: What is the management of heterotopic pregnancy in the source notes?
questions.exp: Heterotopic pregnancy is managed surgically. (Book p439)

questions.q: What type of pregnancy is cornual pregnancy in the source comparison?
questions.exp: Cornual pregnancy is an ectopic pregnancy. (Book p440)

questions.q: What type of pregnancy is angular pregnancy in the source comparison?
questions.exp: Angular pregnancy is intrauterine. (Book p440)

questions.q: Where can a cornual pregnancy implant according to the notes?
opts: Near the uterine angle only inside cavity
Interstitial fallopian tube or rudimentary uterine horn
questions.exp: Cornual ectopic is in the tubal interstitium or rudimentary horn. (Book p440)

questions.q: Where is angular pregnancy located?
opts: Near the angle/cornua of the uterus
In the tubal interstitium lateral to round ligament
questions.exp: Angular pregnancy is intrauterine near the uterine angle/cornua. (Book p440)

questions.q: How does cornual pregnancy relate to the round ligament?
questions.exp: Cornual pregnancy is lateral to the round ligament. (Book p440)

questions.q: How does angular pregnancy relate to the round ligament?
questions.exp: Angular pregnancy is medial to the round ligament. (Book p440)

questions.q: Which cervical finding is part of Paalman criteria?
opts: Internal os open and external os closed
Internal os closed and external os partially open
questions.exp: Paalman criteria include a closed internal os and partially open external os. (Book p440)

questions.q: Where is the gestational sac attached in Paalman criteria for cervical ectopic?
questions.exp: In cervical ectopic, the sac is attached to the endocervix. (Book p440)

questions.q: What symptom is part of Paalman criteria for cervical ectopic?
questions.exp: Cervical ectopic presents with bleeding without uterine cramps. (Book p440)

questions.q: Which finding is part of Spiegelberg criteria for ovarian ectopic?
opts: Normal ovaries with sac in ampulla
Sac present in the ovary with normal tubes
Sac in endocervix with open internal os
questions.exp: Spiegelberg requires sac in ovary and normal tubes. (Book p440)

questions.q: How is the gestational sac related to the uterus in Spiegelberg criteria?
questions.exp: Spiegelberg criteria include sac attached to uterus by ovarian ligament. (Book p440)

questions.q: What histologic finding confirms ovarian ectopic under Spiegelberg criteria?
opts: Ovarian tissue in the gestational sac
Decidua only with no ovarian tissue
questions.exp: Ovarian tissue must be identified in the gestational sac. (Book p440)

questions.q: Which are Studdiford criteria for primary abdominal ectopic pregnancy?
opts: Sac in ampulla with yolk sac
No uteroperitoneal fistula, normal tubes/ovaries, and pregnancy attached to peritoneum
Open internal os and sac in endocervix
Sac in ovary with ovarian tissue
questions.exp: Studdiford requires no uteroperitoneal fistula, normal tubes/ovaries, and peritoneal attachment. (Book p440)

questions.q: Which abdominal ectopic is more common according to the note?
questions.exp: Secondary abdominal ectopic is more common. (Book p440)

questions.q: Which two entities are grouped as molar pregnancy/hydatidiform mole?
questions.exp: Molar pregnancy/hydatidiform mole is partial or complete mole. (Book p441)

questions.q: Which is a form of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia?
questions.exp: Invasive mole is a gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. (Book p441)

questions.q: Which malignant trophoblastic condition is listed under GTN?
questions.exp: Choriocarcinoma is listed under gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. (Book p441)

questions.q: Which tumors are listed under GTN besides invasive mole and choriocarcinoma?
opts: Placental-site trophoblastic tumor and epithelioid trophoblastic tumor
questions.exp: PSTT and ETT are listed GTN tumors. (Book p441)

questions.q: What is the most important risk factor for molar pregnancy?
questions.exp: Previous molar pregnancy is the most important risk factor. (Book p441)

questions.q: Which demographic factors are listed for molar pregnancy?
opts: Only European origin and middle age
Southeast Asian origin and extremes of age
questions.exp: Southeast Asian countries and extremes of age are listed risk factors. (Book p441)

questions.q: What pathologic processes are listed in molar pregnancy?
opts: Undue trophoblastic proliferation and hydropic degeneration
questions.exp: Molar pregnancy involves undue trophoblast proliferation and hydropic degeneration. (Book p441)

questions.q: What distinguishes partial from complete mole by fetal tissue?
opts: Partial mole has some fetal tissue; complete mole has no fetal tissue
Complete mole has fetal tissue; partial has none
Both always have a normal fetus
questions.exp: Some fetal tissue is present in partial mole; no fetal tissue in complete mole. (Book p441)

questions.q: How is molar pregnancy characterized biologically?
opts: A benign disease with malignant potential
A strictly nonneoplastic condition with no follow-up relevance
questions.exp: Molar pregnancy is benign but has malignant potential. (Book p441)

questions.q: What is the most common presentation of molar pregnancy?
opts: Palmar itching in the third trimester
P/V bleeding in the first or early second trimester
questions.exp: P/V bleeding in first/early second trimester is the most common presentation. (Book p441)

questions.q: What vaginal finding is classically associated with molar pregnancy?
questions.exp: Grape-like vesicles P/V are characteristic. (Book p441)

questions.q: Why can PIH develop before 20 weeks in molar pregnancy?
questions.exp: Early-onset PIH before 20 weeks is due to increased placental tissue. (Book p441)

questions.q: Which symptoms/findings are driven by elevated hCG in molar pregnancy?
opts: Hyperemesis, thyrotoxicosis, and bilateral theca-lutein cysts
Hypoglycemia, low TSH, and renal failure only
questions.exp: Raised hCG is associated with hyperemesis, thyrotoxicosis, and bilateral theca-lutein cysts. (Book p441)

questions.q: What can cause pulmonary embolism and breathlessness in molar pregnancy according to the notes?
questions.exp: Pulmonary embolism and breathlessness are attributed to vesicles in the source notes. (Book p441)
